Disney+ and Hulu Raises Prices Again, the Fourth Hike in Four Years

 Sep 23, 2026 8:05am PT 

# Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, the Fourth Hike in Four Years 

 By Todd Spangler 

 

 ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection 

 The streamflation trend continues: Disney is once again asking Disney+ and Hulu subscribers to pay even more for the streaming service.

 Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium, the plans without ads, are both increasing from $18.99 to $21.49/month, up 13%. The pricing strategy is clearly aimed at pushing consumers toward bundles: The Disney+/Hulu Premium bundle is ticking up two bucks, from $19.99 to $21.99/month, which is nearly half what it would cost if you bought them separately. 

 The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu (SVOD only) standalone plans are also getting a hike, from $11.99 to $12.49/month. The Disney+ and Hulu (with ads) bundle remains unchanged at $12.99/month — just 50 cents more than each of the services if purchased separately. The company also is raising the price of the Hulu + Live TV packages and Disney+/Hulu bundles that include ESPN Select (see table below). 

### Popular on Variety 

 The Disney+ and Hulu price increases are effective Wednesday (Sept. 23) for new subscribers. Existing customers will see the new pricing on their next monthly bill. The higher prices come as Pixar blockbuster “Toy Story 5” debuted on Disney+ on Wednesday. 

 Meanwhile, Disney also recently raised the price of the ESPN Unlimited service, which increased from $29.99 to $31.99/month effective Sept. 17.

 Disney’s streaming price hikes have become an annual ritual. The latest increases mark the fourth time in four years the Mouse House is raising rates in the U.S., after price hikes for Disney+ and Hulu in October 2024 and in October 2023. 

 The ad-free Disney+ tier has now nearly doubled in price from the $10.99/month rate in 2023 prior to the fall increase that year.

 Here’s summary of the current U.S. pricing for Disney+, Hulu, Hulu + Live TV and different multiservice bundles as of Sept. 23:

# Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, Ad-Free Plans Now $21.49

Wednesday September 23, 2026 12:10 pm PDT by Juli Clover

Disney today increased the prices on several of its Disney+ and Hulu streaming plans, with the increase coming exactly one year after Disney's last price hike.

 Premium ad-free plans are $2 to $2.50 more expensive per month, while Disney's ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans are $0.50 higher per month. The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle has not changed in price, and that's what Disney is steering customers toward.

- Disney+ (Ads) - $12.49, up from $11.99
- Disney+ (No Ads) - $21.49, up from $18.99
- Hulu (Ads) - $12.49, up from $11.99
- Hulu (No Ads) - $21.49, up from $18.99
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (Ads) - $12.99, no change
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (No Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+, ESPN, Hulu Bundle (Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+ (No Ads), Hulu (No Ads), ESPN Select (Ads) - $32.99, up from $29.99
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Basic (Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Basic (No Ads) - $34.99, up from $32.99

Bundles with ESPN or HBO Max are also $2 to $3 more expensive. Buying a standalone Disney+ or Hulu plan is just $0.50 cheaper per month than getting a bundle, both with ads and without. Disney is pushing bundles because it has been merging Hulu content into the Disney+ app to create an all-in-one experience.

When Disney+ launched in November 2019, it was priced at $6.99 per month. It did not have ads at the time, with Disney introducing its first ad-supported plan in 2022. Pricing for the no-ad option has increased more than 200% in nearly seven years.

Apple's streaming TV service launched right around the same time as Disney+ for $4.99 per month. Today, the Apple TV service is $14.99 per month, also a 200% increase. Other streaming services like Netflix and HBO Max raise prices regularly too.

Disney's higher prices go into effect for new subscribers today, and for existing subscribers on their next monthly bill.

# Disney+ and Hulu Are Raising Prices Again — the Ad-Free Bundle Hits $21.99

Disney+ and Hulu raised U.S. prices on September 23. See every new monthly price and how much the $21.99 premium bundle still saves.

By Lane Mercer Sep 23, 2026

Disney+ and Hulu cost more in the United States starting September 23. Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium now cost $21.49 each per month, while the ad-free bundle that includes both services has increased to $21.99.

The bundle is still far cheaper than paying for both premium plans separately, but subscribers who chose streaming to avoid cable-size bills now face another increase.

## What are the new Disney+ and Hulu prices?

- Disney+ with ads: $12.49 per month.
- Disney+ Premium without ads: $21.49 per month or $214.99 per year.
- Hulu with ads: $12.49 per month.
- Hulu Premium without ads: $21.49 per month.
- Disney+ and Hulu with ads: $12.99 per month.
- Disney+ and Hulu Premium: $21.99 per month.

Disney+ Premium rose from $18.99 to $21.49, and the premium Disney+ and Hulu bundle moved from $19.99 to $21.99.

The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle remains at $12.99. ESPN Select bundles now start at $21.99 with ads and $32.99 for the premium version. ESPN Unlimited bundles remain at $35.99 and $44.99.

The Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle now costs $21.99 per month in the United States. Credits Image: Disney.

## When will subscribers pay the higher price?

New subscribers see the updated prices immediately. Existing monthly subscribers will be charged the new amount on their next billing date after September 23. Annual Disney+ Premium customers will see the change when their plan renews.

Subscribers should check the exact plan name before changing anything. The $12.99 ad-supported bundle did not increase, while several standalone and premium options did.

## Does the bundle still save money?

Yes. Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium would cost $42.98 per month if purchased separately. The $21.99 bundle saves $20.99 each month. The ad-supported bundle saves $11.99 compared with buying both $12.49 plans separately.

Disney is also moving more Hulu programming into Disney+ and plans a unified app by the end of 2026. Hulu still remains available as a standalone service. Disney is combining more of the two services while charging more for most individual plans.

# Disney+ ad-free climbs to $21.49 as Hulu prices rise again

Peter Holden

September 25, 2026

 Disney+ Premium jumps $2.50 to $21.49, but one bundle stays at $12.99 

 DisneyPlus 

Halloween is in October but Disney+ has already geared up to give your wallet a shock with yet another price hike. Yes, your streaming bill is going up again, and this time ad-free Disney+ crosses the $20 mark. Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium now cost $21.49 a month each, up $2.50, and existing subscribers will see the change from October 21.

### What's new

Disney

The new prices are already live for anyone signing up since September 23. If you're an existing subscriber, the increase lands on your first billing cycle on or after October 21.

The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans are going up too, rising 50 cents to $12.49 a month each. The Disney+ Premium annual plan climbs from $189.99 to $214.99.

### Why it matters

Disney is making standalone subscriptions look like a bad deal, and that seems to be the point. The Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle now costs $21.99, which is just 50 cents more than paying for one of those services on its own.

The same trick works at the cheaper end. The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle stays at $12.99, only 50 cents above a single ad-supported plan, so anyone paying for either service standalone is leaving Hulu or Disney+ on the table.

### How the prices stack up

Disney

For perspective, Disney+ launched in 2019 at $6.99 a month. Premium was $15.99 before last October's hike, so ad-free subscribers are now paying $5.50 more a month than they were a year ago.

Here's where the main plans land:

| Disney+, Hulu, & ESPN Bundle plans | Services | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+, Hulu Bundle | Disney+ (With Ads)Hulu (With Ads) | Monthly: $12.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium | Disney+ (No Ads)**Hulu (No Ads) | Monthly: $21.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle | Disney+ (With Ads)**Hulu (With Ads)ESPN Select (With Ads) | Monthly: $21.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle Premium | Disney+ (No Ads)**Hulu (No Ads)ESPN Select (With Ads) | Monthly: $32.99 |
| Disney+ Premium, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle Legacy | Disney+ (No Ads)**Hulu (With Ads)ESPN Select (With Ads) Please note this plan is no longer available to purchase or switch into on Disney+. Existing subscribers will be able to keep their plan so long as they do not cancel or change it. | Monthly: $27.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle | Disney+ (With Ads)Hulu (With Ads)ESPN Unlimited (With Ads) | Monthly: $35.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium | Disney+ (No Ads)**Hulu (No Ads)ESPN Unlimited (With Ads) | Monthly: $44.99 |

Hulu + Live TV packages are getting more expensive as well. If you subscribe through Google Play or another third-party billing partner, Disney notes your price may differ from what it lists directly.

### What isn't changing

The Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Unlimited bundles hold at $35.99 with ads and $44.99 ad-free. Bundles with NFL+ Premium and Disney+ add-ons are also untouched this time around.

### Takeaway

Disney says the extra money goes toward enhancing its streaming platforms, and it'll be interesting to see whether subscribers feel that improvement before next year's increase rolls around. Unfortunately, annual hikes now look like a fixture of the service rather than an exception. If you're on a standalone plan, switching to a bundle before October 21 is the easiest way to get more for roughly the same money.

The Disney+ and Hulu ad-free bundle rises to $21.99 a month - The Money Overview

# The Disney+ and Hulu ad-free bundle rises to $21.99 a month

 By Tyler Foster 

 Published September 25, 2026 

 Image Credit: Raimond Spekking - CC BY-SA 4.0/Wiki Commons 

The Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium, the ad-free package that combines both apps, rose to $21.99 a month this week, a two-dollar increase from $19.99. The new figure means two full, ad-free streaming services together now cost only fifty cents more than Disney+ Premium costs on its own, a gap that has been shrinking with every round of increases Disney has applied to its ad-free lineup. For a household weighing whether a stand-alone app or the bundle makes more financial sense, that fifty-cent spread is the number worth checking, not the two-dollar increase drawing the headlines.

## Two ad-free apps now cost fifty cents more than one

The Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium costs $21.99 a month, only fifty cents more than the $21.49 that Disney+ Premium costs by itself, without Hulu attached at all. Subtracting one figure from the other leaves a narrow premium for adding an entire second, ad-free streaming service on top of an existing Disney+ Premium subscription, a discount for the second app that would have been unthinkable back when the two apps were sold only as separate products with no bundle option at all.

Disney’s pricing page shows why that spread narrowed this round rather than widened: Disney+ Premium’s own standalone price rose by a larger $2.50, while the bundle premium climbed a smaller $2.00, from $19.99 to $21.99. The bundle therefore absorbed a smaller increase in raw dollars even though it already bundles two full services together, the opposite of what a subscriber might expect from a package Disney could just as easily have repriced more aggressively than a single app.

The bundle’s path has tracked the standalone plans closely rather than moving on its own schedule: this is the same round that industry analytics firm eMarketer counted as Disney’s fourth consecutive annual increase to its ad-free streaming lineup, following an October 2025 round that had already pushed the bundle premium to its prior $19.99 figure. A bundle subscriber has therefore absorbed four straight increases on the same package, just as a standalone subscriber has on a single app.

The line items a streaming bill doesn’t have: A bundle’s new rate lands automatically on each subscriber’s own billing date, with nothing to apply for. Property-tax relief isn’t automatic: see the circuit-breaker credit for renters and the heating, cooling and home-repair help in The Senior Property Tax & Home-Cost Relief Kit.

## Disney left its priciest bundle untouched while raising the ones beneath it

Not every bundle moved this round. The Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundle, Disney’s most expensive package, held steady at $35.99 a month with ads and $44.99 without them, according to Hulu’s own sign-up page, even as the two smaller bundles beneath it both rose. The Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select bundle, which pairs the two streaming apps with ESPN’s lower-cost sports tier rather than its full one, increased alongside the standalone plans, moving from $29.99 to $32.99 for the ad-free version and from $19.99 to $21.99 with ads.

The gap between those two figures narrowed rather than widened in the process: for eleven dollars more than Disney+ Premium’s standalone $21.49, a subscriber adds not just Hulu but ESPN’s Select sports tier as well, a spread this round’s increases pulled closer together instead of pushing apart. Leaving the top-tier Unlimited bundle untouched kept the most expensive package from drawing attention this round, even as every subscriber one tier below it took on a larger bill.

The pattern extends the logic already visible in the standalone plans: Disney is raising the price of watching without ads faster than the price of watching with them, and doing so unevenly across its bundle lineup r

End the pricing tricks. Just combine Disney+ and Hulu already | PCWorld

 by Jared Newman Contributor 

# End the pricing tricks. Just combine Disney+ and Hulu already

 News Analysis Sep 25, 2026

## If you're paying separately for either service, you're getting ripped off by design. 

 

 Credit: Jared Newman / Foundry 

Disney doesn’t seem to think too highly of its individual Disney+ and Hulu subscribers.

That’s the only explanation for its latest price hikes, which largely eliminate any reason to pay for either service separately. Oh, Disney will still let you do it, but you’ll only be saving 50 cents per month versus the bundle of Disney+ and Hulu together. The a la carte route is a rip-off by design, intended to make Disney’s bundles look more attractive.

If Disney had a little more respect for its customers, it would just end this charade and combine Disney+ and Hulu already. Instead, it’s made the cynical calculation that the appearance of a deal is better for business.

## Disney’s latest price hikes

See if you can spot the pattern in Disney’s September 2026 price hikes:

- Disney+ (with ads): $11.99 → $12.49/mo.
- Hulu (with ads): $11.99 → $12.49/mo.
- Disney+ and Hulu bundle (with ads): Still $12.99/mo.
- Disney+ (no ads): $18.99 → $21.49/mo.
- Hulu (no ads): $18.99 → $21.49/mo.
- Disney+ and Hulu bundle (no ads): $19.99 → $21.99/mo.

(If you’re bundling Disney+, Hulu, and HBO Max, those prices quietly ticked upward this week as well. The trio rose from $19.99 to $21.99 per month with ads, or $32.99 to $34.99 without. The cost of Hulu + Live TV also rose from $90 to $100 per month when bundled with Disney+, Hulu on-demand, and ESPN Unlimited.)

With the new pricing, paying for just Disney+ or Hulu is a mere 50 cents per month cheaper than combining them, down from $1 per month savings previously. While Disney has obviously been pushing customers toward bundles for some time, the latest price hikes squeeze the a la carte savings down to farcical levels.

## The Hulu-Disney+ merger plan

Disney has already made clear its intention to mash Disney+ and Hulu into a single app. If you subscribe to both services, you can now access most of Hulu’s catalog through Disney+, with an option to sync your Hulu profile to port over your watchlist and viewing history.

And while Disney has not committed to a timeline for discontinuing the Hulu app, it’s become an afterthought as the company pushes people over to the Disney+ experience. One employee told Business Insider‘s James Faris that Hulu’s app is now “on life support, with no active development.”

Strangely, though, Disney has insisted that it will keep selling standalone Hulu and Disney+ subscriptions, even if Hulu’s app goes away. With the latest price hikes, you have to wonder why it would even bother.

The charitable view is that Disney doesn’t want to push happy Hulu subscribers out of their current subscriptions and into an unfamiliar app. It also hasn’t ported Hulu’s live TV service into Disney+ yet, so it can’t wind down Hulu’s own app until that happens.

But I propose a more cynical explanation: By keeping individual Hulu and Disney+ subscriptions around, Disney gets to crow about the savings you get from combining them. Never mind that those inflated savings come from pushing standalone prices to comical levels, or that bundle pricing continues to rise as well. Instead, Disney can point to the value of getting two services basically for the price of one.

## The bundle savings are a ruse

Sadly this outcome was predictable a couple of years ago, as more streamers started bundling their services together. It was easy to see then how standalone prices would rise at much faster rate than bundled pricing, giving customers the feeling of getting a deal even if it’s on services they don’t really want.

# Disney+ and Hulu Price Increase 2026: New Costs

Disney+ and Hulu ad-free plans jump to $21.49 on October 21, 2026. See every new price, which bundle stayed flat, and how to cut your bill.

Sam Carter Sep 24, 2026 8 min read

Photo: Anthony Quintano / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

Disney just raised the price of Disney+ and Hulu for the fourth time in four years, and this time the ad-free plans take the biggest hit: $2.50 a month each. The good news is buried in the fine print. One bundle did not go up at all, and for most households it is now the obvious plan to be on.

Quick answer

Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium (no ads) rise from $18.99 to $21.49 a month. The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans go from $11.99 to $12.49, and the ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle goes from $19.99 to $21.99. New subscribers pay the new prices now; existing subscribers see them on their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stays at $12.99.

## Key takeaways

- Ad-free standalone plans jump 13%. Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium both go to $21.49 a month.
- Existing subscribers have until October 21, 2026 before the new rate lands on a bill. New sign-ups pay it immediately.
- The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is frozen at $12.99. It now costs just 50 cents more than either app on its own.
- ESPN bundles are split. The ESPN Select bundles rise $2 to $3, while the ESPN Unlimited bundles stay at $35.99 and $44.99.
- If you pay for ad-free Disney+ alone, the ad-free Duo bundle is only 50 cents more and adds all of Hulu.

## Every new Disney+ and Hulu price

These are the US monthly prices announced on September 23, 2026. Find your line, compare it with your current bill, and skip ahead to the fixes.

| Plan | Old price | New price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ Basic (with ads) | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Disney+ Premium (no ads) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu (with ads) | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Hulu Premium (no ads) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Disney+ and Hulu bundle (with ads) | $12.99 | $12.99 | No change |
| Disney+ and Hulu bundle (no ads) | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select (with ads) | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Premium (no ads) | $29.99 | $32.99 | +$3.00 |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited (with ads) | $35.99 | $35.99 | No change |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Premium (no ads) | $44.99 | $44.99 | No change |

Disney also said it is raising Hulu + Live TV packages that include ESPN Select, but the individual live TV figures vary by package. If you pay for Hulu + Live TV, the exact new amount will be in the notice email Disney started sending this week, and it will also show under your account's subscription page before the change takes effect.

For context, Disney+ launched in November 2019 at $6.99 a month. The ad-free plan now costs more than three times that, and the service has gone up every year since 2022.

Photo: Anthony Quintano / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

## When your bill actually changes

This is the only part of the announcement that affects what you pay this month, so it is worth getting right.

| Who you are | When the new price applies |
| --- | --- |
| New subscriber (signing up today) | Immediately, as of September 23, 2026 |
| Existing monthly subscriber | Your first billing date on or after October 21, 2026 |
| Billed through Apple, Google, Amazon, or Roku | Same timing, but the app store sends its own consent notice |
| Billed through a carrier or partner (Verizon, Xfinity, etc.) | Set by the partner; check your partner bill or email |

Some early reports said the new rates applied on September 23 for everyone. That date only covers new customers. If you already subscribe directly with Disney, your next bill before October 21 stays at the old price.

If you pay through Apple's App Store, you may be asked to accept the increase in a pop-up.

# Disney+ Plans Compared: Every Plan, Bundle and Add-on Price, October 2026

Disney+ is $12.49 with ads, Premium $21.49 or $214.99 a year, the Hulu bundle $12.99 or $21.99, ESPN bundles to $44.99, NFL+ bundles $45.99 up. Every price on one page.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Disney+ has two plans of its own and nine more that wrap it with Hulu, ESPN, HBO Max or NFL+. As of October 10, 2026, Disney+‘s plans and prices page lists Disney+ (With Ads) at $12.49 a month, Disney+ Premium at $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year, the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99 or $21.99, the ESPN bundles from $21.99 to $44.99, the HBO Max bundles at $21.99 or $34.99, and two NFL+ Premium bundles at $45.99 and $54.99. These are the prices for new subscriptions since September 23, 2026; the page says anyone who signed up earlier sees the change “in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.” This guide puts every price on one page, works out the arithmetic Disney’s page does not, and notes where the page is silent. If you are leaving, the billing paths are in our Disney+ cancellation guide.

## The quick answer

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49 a month, no annual option listed
- Disney+ Premium (No Ads): $21.49 a month, or $214.99 a year ($17.92 a month by our math)
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle: $12.99 with ads, $21.99 with no ads on both, 50 cents over Disney+ alone
- With ESPN: $21.99 or $32.99 with ESPN Select, $35.99 or $44.99 with ESPN Unlimited
- With HBO Max: $21.99 with ads, $34.99 with no ads, direct billing only
- With NFL+ Premium: $45.99 or $54.99, on the ESPN Unlimited bundles only
- Extra Member: $6.99 to $14.99 a month depending on plan
- Free trial: none. “Please note that Disney+ does not currently offer a free trial.”

Hulu costs $12.49 a month with ads and $21.49 a month without ads in the US after Disney's latest price rise. New subscribers pay that now; existing members move on their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Hulu + Live TV is $99.99 a month with ads.

Here is the twist that most price guides miss: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads costs $12.99, just 50 cents more than Hulu on its own, and the ad-free bundle is $21.99, also 50 cents more than ad-free Hulu. For almost everyone, buying Hulu by itself no longer makes sense. This guide covers every plan, what you actually get, the bundles, student and carrier deals, price history and who should pay for what.

Prices checked October 2, 2026

Prices from Disney's September 23, 2026 US price announcement: Hulu with ads $12.49 (was $11.99), Hulu Premium (no ads) $21.49 (was $18.99), Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads $12.99 (unchanged), bundle Premium $21.99 (was $19.99), Hulu + Live TV $99.99 with ads or $109.99 without (both up $10). Hulu's US plan page was geo-blocked from our test location, so we confirmed these against multiple reports of Disney's announcement.

The short answer

- Hulu with ads: $12.49 a month. The bundle with Disney+ is $12.99. Buy the bundle.
- Hulu Premium (no ads): $21.49. The ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle is $21.99. Again, buy the bundle.
- Students: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is $6.49; the older $1.99 Hulu-only student plan may not be open to new signups.
- Hulu + Live TV: $99.99 with ads, and it already includes Disney+ and ESPN.
- Hulu has raised prices every October since 2021. Plan on another rise in late 2027.

## Hulu plans and what you get

| Monthly price | $12.49 | $21.49 | $99.99 with ads, $109.99 ad-free on-demand |
| Yearly cost | $149.88 | $257.88 | $1,199.88 |
| Ads | Yes | Almost none (see below) | On live channels |
| Screens at once | 2 | 2 | 2 (unlimited with add-on) |
| Downloads | No | Yes | On-demand library only |
| 4K | Select titles | Select titles | Select titles |
| Live channels | No | No | 95+ channels, cloud DVR |
| Includes Disney+ and ESPN | No | No | Yes |

### The fine print

- "No ads" is not quite no ads. A handful of shows on Hulu Premium still play short ads before and after episodes because of licensing deals. Hulu lists them with a "no ads" exception. It is a few titles, not a lot, but it surprises people.
- No downloads on the ad plan. Offline viewing is Premium-only.
- Two screens. Families with three or four TVs need the Unlimited Screens add-on, which is only available with Hulu + Live TV.
- The Hulu app is moving into Disney+. During 2026 Disney is folding Hulu content into the Disney+ app. Standalone Hulu plans are still sold, but more and more of the experience lives in Disney+, which is another reason the bundle makes sense.
- Price rises apply to existing members after a 30-day notice. There is no grandfathering.
